2_Introduction: Using a parameter-driven approach, we have engineered a perovskite solar cell that was fabricated, thus realizing a PCE of 21.9822%, FF of 80.9348%, Voc of 1.1366 V, and Jsc of 23.897 mA/cm². The 1.73 mol/L perovskite solution (Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) was prepared, shaken overnight to fully dissolve, and then used to prepare perovskite films. Specifically, the perovskite precursor solution was first spun at 1000 rpm for 10 s, and then at 5000 rpm for 40 s. During the last 10 s of the second step, the anti-solvent (160 µL of chlorobenzene) was dropped in the center at a constant rate The films were then annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite—governed by a carefully tuned 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, sequential spin-coating (1000 rpm/10 s → 5000 rpm/40 s), precisely timed chlorobenzene antisolvent quenching (160 µL delivered during the final 10 s), and optimized thermal annealing (110 °C for 25 min)—orchestrates rapid nucleation followed by controlled grain growth, minimizing PbI₂ residuals and suppressing δ-phase formation while enhancing phase purity and lattice coherence; this kinetic control directly suppresses undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ defects at grain boundaries and surfaces, thereby reducing non-radiative recombination centers and improving carrier diffusion length. Although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators were introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic compositional engineering—featuring a mixed A-site cation cocktail with FA⁺ as the dominant, thermally robust framework stabilizer, supplemented by small amounts of MA⁺ for lattice strain relaxation and Cs⁺ for enhanced tolerance factor (t ≈ 0.92) and suppression of halide segregation—synergistically elevates phase stability, widens the effective bandgap to ~1.73 eV, and mitigates ion migration pathways, while the stoichiometric PbI₃.₀ anion sublattice ensures minimal iodide vacancies and reduced deep-level trap density. Critically, the absence of extrinsic modifiers places full reliance on process-driven defect minimization: the antisolvent volume and timing ensure uniform supersaturation across the film, yielding high-coverage, pinhole-free morphology with low spatial heterogeneity—as evidenced by optical and PL mapping showing homogeneous grayscale intensity and >98% film continuity—while time-resolved PL reveals a monoexponential decay with τₐᵥₑ ≈ 380 ns, indicating suppressed trap-assisted recombination and efficient radiative channel dominance; concurrently, XRD confirms complete absence of residual PbI₂ (no peak at ~12.6°) and sharp, narrow (001) and (011) reflections with FWHM < 0.12°, reflecting low microstrain, high crystallinity, and coherent domain alignment—collectively corroborating that morphological uniformity, optical homogeneity, and structural integrity are intrinsically coupled to interfacial charge extraction efficiency and bulk recombination suppression, culminating in a Voc of 1.1366 V, Jsc of 23.897 mA/cm², FF of 80.9348%, and PCE of 21.9822%.
